bundle: WI-7 / L-038 residual — debt-component period alignment, cash-side period alignment, preference capital
question: Three residual questions were left open by §17.18: DEBT-COMPONENT-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT, CASH-SIDE-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT and PREFERENCE_CAPITAL. Can any of them be closed by existing primary evidence and current governed contracts, or does each require an explicit register-owner/policy decision?
notRepeated: the caption search over both Marico reports (483 pages; source/caption-search-log.txt) — its result is cited, not re-run
the Note 13(a) current-maturities recovery and the one-cell dataset correction carried by §17.18
the WI-7 payload / superseded-payload analysis and the §17.15 arithmetic correction
the L-039 finding (a different issuer, a different question); it is not touched here

residuals.invariantEvidence: capitalStructure.ts header rule 3 and grossDebtOf() line 121: all four debt components must resolve to one period end, and the refusal the payload publishes (NOT_COMPUTABLE / PERIOD_MISMATCH) is that rule doing its job on two instants (ST 383 @2024-03-31, LL 145 @2024-03-31, LT 2 @2023-03-31, CM 0 @2023-03-31).
residuals.evidence: At 2023-03-31 every required input carries a filed number at that one instant: LT 2, ST 473, CM 0 (printed zero), leases 133, cash 207, current investments 578, all from the FY2023-24 report's comparative column (MARICO-INDAS-CONSOL-FY24-AR-COMPARATIVE). Driven with only that period, the unmodified contract computes grossDebt 608 crore, cashAndInvestments 785 crore and netDebt −177 crore. Nothing was relaxed, carried forward or substituted for that run.
residuals.refinesRegister: §17.18 states that −177 crore 'is not a value the governed path can produce; it is a hypothetical'. That is true of the published configuration and untrue of the code: the same code produces it when the block is anchored at that instant. The register sentence is left as written and the refinement recorded in §17.22.

decisionRequired.question: May the capital-structure block be anchored at an earlier annual instant than the newest one, when that instant is the only one at which the required components are complete — and if so, under what label?
subQuestions: Which instant is chosen when more than one is complete (newest complete instant, or the instant of the valuation's own price/earnings inputs)?
How is a block anchored earlier than the assessment's data cut labelled in the payload, so that a reader cannot mistake it for the FY2024 position?
May an enterprise value computed from FY2024 fundamentals be converted to equity with a FY2023 net-debt figure, or must the whole assessment be re-anchored?
Does the same latitude apply to lease liabilities, whose treatment is period-sensitive (IND AS 116)?
consequencesIfTaken: period mixing moves from the component level, where the contract refuses it today, to the block level, where it would then be published
EV, leverage and every per-share leg inherit the anchor; the numbers would differ by publication rule rather than by evidence
Marico would publish a net-debt figure at 2023-03-31 while its price and earnings inputs are FY2024/FY2026 — a mixed-date payload
consequencesIfRefused: the debt side stays NOT_COMPUTABLE / PERIOD_MISMATCH at the published instant
the FY2023 figure remains an evidence-backed observation that no governed output publishes
decisionRequired.whyNotAlone: even with netDebt present at 2023-03-31 the probe still reports preferenceCapital MISSING / NOT_REPORTED, so the enterprise-to-equity bridge remains blocked.
decisionRequired.owner: register owner for the capital-structure aggregation contract (R-4.1 / IID-2 lineage), on the IID limitation register; not the investigation, and not a code change.

residuals.mechanism: capitalStructure.ts line 224 sums cash and current investments with sum(), which checks presence only; line 225 subtracts the sum from grossDebt. No period is compared on the cash side, neither between the two cash components nor against the debt side.
residuals.reachabilityEvidence: A two-instant fixture (debt complete @2024-03-31, cash only @2023-03-31) publishes grossDebt 528 crore, cashAndInvestments 785 crore and netDebt −257 crore — a net-debt number built from two balance sheets (runs/01-probe.txt, B-1). The fixture is synthetic and no Marico figure is taken from it.
residuals.corpusScan: 9 committed datasets: 2 resolve both sides to one instant, 5 have the debt side blocked (so the cash rule is never reached), 2 have an incomplete cash side. 0 would publish cross-period net debt today (runs/03-cash-side-corpus-scan.txt).

decisionRequired.question: Should the same-instant rule be extended from the four debt components to the cash side — cash against current investments, and the cash side against the debt side — and what should the block publish when they disagree?
decisionRequired.recommendedShapeIfAuthorised: publish the components as they resolve, refuse netDebt with NOT_COMPUTABLE / PERIOD_MISMATCH and a note naming the two instants; no new value, no substitution, no change to any currently published figure (0 datasets affected)
consequencesIfTaken: the latent cross-period publication is closed
a future issuer whose cash or investments resolve to a different instant would lose netDebt instead of silently gaining a wrong one
consequencesIfRefused: the gap stays latent; nothing in the committed corpus publishes a cross-period figure today
decisionRequired.owner: register owner for the capital-structure aggregation contract (same owner as above)

residuals.whyNotImplementedHere: the work item's authority forbids altering capitalStructure.ts or introducing a new period-alignment rule without explicit authority; a test that pinned today's behaviour would enshrine the defect and a test that forbade it would be the fix.

residuals.whyNoNewSource: the caption search over both reports (483 pages) is complete for 'preference share' and every hit is the same authorised-capital table; this environment has no egress to the issuer or exchange hosts and no PDF tooling, so no unread page could be retrieved here in any case.
residuals.reread: FY2023-24 Note 12(a), PDF p.189 (the only extracted share-capital page): the preference class exists ONLY in I Authorised share capital (7 crore shares, ₹65 crore); II Issued, subscribed and paid-up lists equity shares only (1,29,41,01,828 shares, 129 / 129) with no preference row and no dash; the 'Rights, preferences and restrictions attached to equity shares' paragraph enumerates 150 crore equity ₹1 + 8 crore equity ₹10 and does not mention the preference class the table above it prints.
residuals.whyTheEnumerationCannotHelp: an enumeration that omits a class the same note prints is unusable in either direction: it neither establishes issued preference capital nor declares it nil, and reading nil from the omission is exactly the inference D-2 forbids.
precedents: WI-5 (eClerx) withdrew a preference-capital nil declared on 'The Company has only one class of equity shares having a par value of Rs 10 per share.' — scoped by its heading to equity shares, so it says nothing about preference capital

the L-035 review record accepted a preference-capital nil (Infosys, 'The Company has only one class of shares referred to as equity shares having a par value of ₹5/-.') only as an explicit cross-scope mapping with acceptedBy recorded; the grammar requires wording, and Marico has no sentence of either shape
residuals.remainingPath: a filing page that prints an issued/paid-up preference row, or that declares the class nil in words (or in the shape the L-035 grammar can bind with a recorded acceptance). That is a retrieval question, not a policy one.
